subject: Demo recap + 15-day trial runway proposal — ArcadiaLane
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Rees <jacob.rees@arcadialane.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + proposed 15-day trial runway — ArcadiaLane

Hi Jacob,

Thanks again for the demo time today — great conversation and very helpful context on the ticket routing & resolution use cases. Quick recap and a proposed trial/POC runway to get to a data-driven decision in ~15 calendar days.

Company problem we discussed:
- High support triage latency and manual resolution for attachments + multi-doc contexts.
- Need sub-250ms p95 for quick routing + high precision on intent classification to avoid downstream false positives.

Proposed 15-day trial (high level) — success criteria and owners:
1) Baseline metrics collected (ArcadiaLane) — avg first-touch handle time, current intent accuracy on sample set. (Owner: ArcadiaLane)
2) Functional success: Redwood model must achieve >=90% precision on the intent classification evaluation set we agree on. (Owner: Redwood SE)
3) Latency SLO: API p95 < 250ms on production-simulated load (Owner: Redwood infra / ArcadiaLane dev)
4) Practical acceptance: For a randomized 500-ticket subset, recommended routing matches human tag in >=88% of cases. (Owner: joint)
5) Budget / cost guardrails: projected incremental inference cost <= $X per 1k tickets (we'll provide estimate).

High-level evaluation plan (attachments: arcadialane-eval-outline.pdf, sample-prompt-set.csv):
- Day 0: Kickoff call (confirm dataset, access, security contacts)
- Days 1–3: Ingest and baseline runs against your sample set; Redwood provides sandbox credentials + monitoring dashboard
- Days 4–10: Iteration — prompt tuning, caching/batching configuration, and model variant tests
- Days 11–13: Stability runs, spike tests, and SLO verification
- Day 14–15: Final evaluation, metrics delivery, and decision review

Immediate asks from you:
- Share a 1k–2k sample of representative tickets (anonymized) and the current routing labels by Apr 30 if possible
- Confirm primary InfoSec contact for sandbox access (we'll need an Okta/SCIM or temporary credentials approach)
- Preferred kickoff window next week (May 3–5) or the week after

Logistics / owners from Redwood:
- Aditya Rao (cc) — SE lead: sandbox onboarding, prompt tuning, performance testing
- Marissa Cole (cc) — Contract & commercial owner (pricing, term questions, potential reserved capacity)
- Chloe Martin — AE (program coordination, timeline)

Attachments: arcadialane-eval-outline.pdf (trial plan & acceptance matrix), sample-prompt-set.csv

Thanks — sending a more technical note from Aditya shortly with the sandbox/endpoint details.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

---
Redwood Inference — production-first inference for LLMs

From: Jacob Rees <jacob.rees@arcadialane.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed 15-day trial runway — ArcadiaLane

Chloe —

Really appreciate the clear plan. We're interested and would like to run the 15-day lane. Quick notes:
- We can provide a 1.2k anonymized ticket sample by Apr 30.
- Preferred kickoff: May 3rd in the morning (PT) — does that work for your team?
- Our InfoSec lead is Lena Park (lena.park@arcadialane.com). She'll be the point for access and any security questionnaires (SOC2 evidence, network allowlists).

Two quick commercial asks up front:
1) Will the trial be under an NDA / SOW or can we use the standard evaluation agreement?
2) If we exceed the trial traffic, is there an overdraft protection or rate limit guardrail?

If you can confirm kickoff + security steps, we'll lock internal stakeholders.

Thanks,
Jacob Rees
Director, Applied AI | ArcadiaLane
jacob.rees@arcadialane.com | +1 617-555-0123

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Rees <jacob.rees@arcadialane.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed 15-day trial runway — ArcadiaLane

Jacob — thanks, this is great. May 3 morning PT works for us — proposing 9:30am PT for kickoff (I'll send a calendar invite).

Answers to your two asks:
1) Trial paperwork: we can run this under a short evaluation agreement / mutual NDA. I'm attaching a standard evaluation outline and I'll loop in Marissa for the commercial/contract step. We can also initiate a DocuSign NDA if that speeds things up: https://docusign.com/some-link/arcadialane-nda
2) Traffic guardrails: yes — sandbox is rate-limited by default. We'll provision a sandbox quota for the trial and Aditya will provide recommended throttles and how to request a temporary bump if needed. Any overages will be reported and require approval before production-level consumption.

Security: we'll share a SOC2 summary and the minimum network steps in the sandbox-endpoint-instructions.txt attachment. Lena can reach out to security@redwood.com and I will make introductions.

HubSpot deal link for your reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ARC-2027-0427

Next steps (I'll own coordination):
- I'll send the calendar invite for May 3, 9:30am PT
- ArcadiaLane to deliver anonymized sample by Apr 30
- Lena to confirm preferred auth flow (Okta SCIM or temporary token)
- Aditya to open the sandbox and share endpoint + keys (expected within 24 hours of kickoff)

Marissa — can you confirm we'll route the standard eval agreement (and flag any commercial approvals if they need reserved capacity later)?

Best,
Chloe

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Rees <jacob.rees@arcadialane.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed 15-day trial runway — ArcadiaLane

Hi Jacob / Chloe,

Quick technical runbook for sandbox so you have visibility before kickoff:
- Sandbox endpoint: https://sandbox-us.redwood-inference.com/arcadialane (temporary API key delivered at kickoff)
- Model variants we'll test: redwood-llama-3-13b (FP16), redwood-llama-3-13b-quant (4-bit) — we'll run small evals to compare latency/quality tradeoffs
- Recommended batch & cache config: start with batch_size=4 for evaluation and enable prefix KV caching for repeated context; we'll tune after baseline
- Tokenization & costs: we'll share a per-model token-cost table in the onboarding doc; rough estimate for 1k tickets is ~ $28–40 depending on variant and batching
- Observability: we'll provide a short dashboard link (post-kickoff) with latency histograms and token breakdown by route

Attachments I will post to the sandbox bucket after kickoff: sandbox-endpoint-instructions.txt (endpoint + auth), and a short prompt-set template (sample-prompt-set.csv).

If you have an internal dev who prefers Postman or Python, here's a one-line curl to sanity-check the endpoint once keys are active:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"input":"Summarize ticket: user cannot login"}' https://sandbox-us.redwood-inference.com/arcadialane/v1/generate

I'll be on the kickoff and will lead the tuning/metrics work.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
